KEY DATES
  Dec 31, 2026   Last payroll date for 2026 retirement-plan salary deferrals
  Jan 15, 2027   Q4 2026 federal estimated tax payment (Form 1040-ES)
  Feb 1, 2027    W-2s to employees and Copy A to SSA; 1099-NEC to recipients and the IRS
                 (Jan 31 falls on a Sunday, so the deadline moves to Monday)
  Feb 1, 2027    Form 941 for Q4 and Form 940 (annual FUTA)
  Mar 1, 2027    Paper 1099-MISC and 1099-INT to the IRS (Mar 31 if you e-file)
  Mar 15, 2027   Partnership (1065) and S corporation (1120-S) returns, and K-1s to owners
  Apr 15, 2027   Individual returns and Q1 2027 estimates

2026 NUMBERS
  Social Security wage base .................. $184,500
  401(k)/403(b) employee deferral ............ $24,500 (+$8,000 catch-up at 50+; $11,250 at ages 60–63)
  Standard deduction ......................... $16,100 single / $32,200 married filing jointly
  Child tax credit ........................... $2,200 per qualifying child
  1099-NEC / 1099-MISC threshold ............. $2,000 for payments made in 2026 (was $600)
  1099-K threshold ........................... back to $20,000 and 200 transactions
  SALT deduction cap ......................... $40,400 (phases down above $505,000 MAGI)

PAYROLL HOUSEKEEPING
  1. Ask every employee to confirm their legal name and mailing address in your payroll portal
     before Dec 1. A mismatch between the W-2 name and the name SSA has on file is the most
     common reason we end up filing W-2c's.
  2. Collect a current W-9 from every contractor you expect to pay $2,000 or more. If a
     contractor won't give you a TIN, backup withholding at 24% applies.
  3. Tips and overtime: the new deductions for qualified tips and overtime pay mean those amounts
     need to be tracked separately in payroll. Check that your provider has this turned on.
  4. Never email us a full Social Security number or EIN. If a form asks for one, type it as
     XXX-XX-XXXX or XX-XXXXXXX and upload the actual document to the client portal instead.
  5. Household employers: wages paid to a nanny or caregiver go on Schedule H with your 1040.
     You'll still need an EIN (not your SSN) on the W-2 you give them.
